Shalini: Preeti!! the biryani at your party is still in my dreams
Shalini: you're honestly better than any caterer in this city
Preeti: that's so sweet, thank you. I loved making it
Shalini: so my brother's engagement is next month... 80 people... you'd be PERFECT. we can pay something
Preeti: I'm really glad you enjoyed it. let me think and check my month, I'll reply by Friday
Shalini: of course!! no pressure
(Friday)
Preeti: I've thought about it. 80 people is too big for my kitchen and my work hours, so I can't take it on. I can make the dessert for the family dinner the night before, if that helps, at my usual home rate
Shalini: ahh ok, that's actually great. thank you for being straight

qa.q: How many people are coming to the engagement?
qa.a: 80 people are coming to the engagement.

qa.q: How did Preeti feel about Shalini's praise?
qa.a: Preeti was genuinely pleased, calling it sweet and saying "I loved making it".

qa.q: What did Preeti do that kept the decision separate from the praise?
qa.a: Preeti thanked Shalini, asked for time until Friday, then judged the request on real limits and offered something manageable.

qa.q: How did Shalini react to Preeti's straight answer?
qa.a: Shalini accepted it warmly, saying the dessert offer was great and thanking Preeti for being straight.

grounding: An adult enjoys Shalini's praise, waits before deciding, and judges the catering request on its merits rather than on the compliments.

passage:
In the kasba panchayat office, Vikas the contractor held out a box of sweets. "Parul-ji, the whole block is talking about you. The youngest group leader, and the smartest. The women's hall will be your legacy. My team can start tomorrow."
Parul smiled and took one sweet. "Thank you, that's kind." She meant it; the words did feel good.
"So I'll bring the papers tonight?"
"Not tonight," she said. "We've asked for three quotes. The group will compare them on Saturday."
His smile thinned a little. On Saturday the women sat with the three papers. His quote was the most expensive and had no completion date. They chose a builder from the next village, and Parul sent Vikas a polite note thanking him for his interest.

qa.q: How many quotes did the group ask for?
How did Parul feel about Vikas's compliments?
qa.a: She was genuinely pleased and meant her thanks, since the words did feel good, but she didn't let them decide anything.
She accepted the kind words, refused to rush, and let the group judge the quotes on price and completion date.

qa.q: How might Vikas feel when his smile thinned?
qa.a: He may have felt disappointed that his praise didn't speed things up, since he wanted the papers signed that night.

grounding: A young group leader enjoys a contractor's flattery but waits and judges his offer on its merits alongside other quotes.
